shill: cellular: remove CellularError::FromChromeosDBusError() This CL is part of a series to remove support of the legacy modem manager (cromo) from shill. CellularError::FromChromeosDBusError() translates D-Bus error from reported by cromo to corresponding shill::Error, which is no longer needed after deprecating the cromo support in shill. A follow-up CL will further simplify CellularError. BUG=chromium:954634 TEST=Run unit tests. shill: cellular: replace MM_MODEM_INTERFACE with MM_DBUS_INTERFACE_MODEM This CL is part of a series to remove support of the legacy modem manager (cromo) from shill. vboot: add vb2_sha.h to replace NEED_VB2_SHA_LIBRARY When clients wish to use SHA functionality, they should import vb2_sha.h header instead of setting NEED_VB2_SHA_LIBRARY and importing vb2_api.h. The latter will be deprecated. NEED_VB2_SHA_LIBRARY is troublesome since the compiler may complain when it is defined multiple times within the same namespace. FROMLIST: ASoC: Intel: avoid Oops if DMA setup fails Currently in sst_dsp_new() if we get an error return from sst_dma_new() we just print an error message and then still complete the function successfully. This means that we are trying to run without sst->dma properly set up, which will result in NULL pointer dereference when sst->dma is later used. This was happening for me in sst_dsp_dma_get_channel(): struct sst_dma *dma = dsp->dma; ... dma->ch = dma_request_channel(mask, dma_chan_filter, dsp); This resulted in: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000018 IP: sst_dsp_dma_get_channel+0x4f/0x125 [snd_soc_sst_firmware] Fix this by adding proper error handling for the case where we fail to set up DMA. (am from https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/20190426164740.211139-1-zwisler@google.com/raw) BUG=b:131111214 TEST=Force error path for failed DMA setup, make sure system recovers Change-Id: Ie9469faa5e10271edfb85cc1bf2c6b76c0856172 Signed-off-by: Ross Zwisler <zwisler@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1586180 Commit-Ready: Ross Zwisler <zwisler@chromium.org> Tested-by: Ross Zwisler <zwisler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Curtis Malainey <cujomalainey@chromium.org>

tast: fix Assistant set volume test failure. Recently there is a continuous test failure in ui.AssistantTextQueries with an error msg: System volume 75 doesn't match the requested volume 25. This is caused by a server side change on volume control, where they narrowed down the volume range from 1-100 to 1-10. Thus, when user try to set the volume with an absolute value beyond 10 (e.g. "Volume 25"), the assistant will punt an out-of-range error message. In this change, we instead set the volume by percentage to be more straightforward and avoid confusion. BUG=None. TEST=tast -verbose run $(DUT) ui.AssistantTextQueries Change-Id: I7a7e527fd41f49a72c7414311989253502bafe31 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1579742 Commit-Ready: Meilin Wang <meilinw@chromium.org> Tested-by: Meilin Wang <meilinw@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Xiaohui Chen <xiaohuic@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>

minigbm: virgl: Map BO_USE_SCANOUT to VIRGL_BIND_SCANOUT Now crosvm use VIRGL_BIND_SCANOUT to decide if we should allocate buffer from host minigbm. For buffers sent to Wayland, they have to be allocated from host minigbm. Since arc-cros-gralloc already maps GRALLOC_USAGE_HW_COMPOSER to BO_USE_SCANOUT, we only need to mark related formats good for BO_USE_SCANOUT and then map BO_USE_SCANOUT to VIRGL_BIND_SCANOUT.
